title: Improved governance for your docs: reviews and expanded roles
summary: Mintlify Enterprise now has stronger governance built into the editor. Require a review before any change goes live, and use expanded roles to control who can write, approve, and publish.
body_markdown:
Mintlify Enterprise now has stronger governance built into the editor. You can require a review within Mintlify before any change goes live, and use expanded and custom roles to control who can write, approve, and publish.


Teams that review in GitHub pull requests can keep doing that. Review in the editor is another option for teammates who don't work in GitHub.


## Require a review before anything ships


If your reviewers already work in pull requests, keep that workflow. Our guide to[docs governance with Git and branch protection](https://www.mintlify.com/library/documentation-governance-with-git-and-branch-protection) covers that setup. If you want reviews to happen in Mintlify, turn on[review before publishing](https://www.mintlify.com/docs/editor/review#require-review-before-publishing) and editors see **Request review** where **Publish** used to be. They pick reviewers, either people or a group.


Reviewers see the changes in a diff, including navigation and site settings, and approve in the editor without opening GitHub. Then a publisher or admin publishes.


Review requests show up in each reviewer's[inbox](https://www.mintlify.com/docs/dashboard/inbox) and email, and the requester gets an inbox item when their changes are approved, so nothing sits waiting unnoticed.


You can also run reviews from your AI tools. Connect the[MCP](https://www.mintlify.com/docs/ai/mintlify-mcp) to Claude, Cursor, or ChatGPT, and ask it to request a review on the pages you changed. Reviewers can approve a request the same way. Once the changes are approved, a publisher or admin can publish them from the editor or through the MCP.


Requiring review turns auto publish off, so nothing reaches your live site until someone approves it. A docs lead, or someone from legal or brand, can sign off on a change right in the editor.


Reviews work on your deployment branch and on branches. On a branch, one approval covers every change, and publishing merges the branch.


Admins can control the rules:


- **Required approvals** : set how many reviewers must approve before a change can publish.
- **Dismiss approvals on new changes** : an approval only covers the version the reviewer saw, so edits after approval need another review.


### Protected deployment branches


If your repo is on GitHub.com and your deployment branch has branch protection, you can still require review. Every review moves to a branch, and admins can't publish without review. When a reviewer has connected their GitHub account, approving in the editor also approves the pull request in GitHub. GitHub's merge checks, such as required status checks, still apply.


Without branch protection, admins can publish their own changes without review.


A few limits today:


- Require review before publishing is in beta.
- It needs a docs repo on GitHub.


## Give everyone the right level of access


We've added three new built-in[roles](https://www.mintlify.com/docs/dashboard/roles) : owner, publisher, and commenter. Here's what each role can do:


Role What it can do


Owner Delete or transfer the organization


Admin Manage members and settings


Publisher Approve reviews and publish


Editor Draft changes and request reviews


Commenter Comment in the editor without editing


Viewer View and preview


Only publishers, admins, and owners can approve and publish, so you can give editor access to a whole team. Commenters can give feedback on a draft without being able to change it.


Owners and admins can create a custom role with the permissions a team needs. If you run more than one docs site, you can also give someone a different role on each, like editor on your API reference and viewer on your help center.


## What changes for existing Enterprise customers


Your members keep the access they had. Existing editors became publishers with the same permissions they had before. Deleting the organization moved from admin to the new owner role.


## What's next


Require review before publishing needs a GitHub repo today. We're working on adding support for GitLab and Bitbucket.


## Get started


1. In the dashboard, open **Settings → Editor → Reviewing** .
2. Turn on **Require review before publishing** . Only admins can change this setting.
3. Open **Settings → Members** and assign publisher, editor, and commenter roles.


See the[review](https://www.mintlify.com/docs/editor/review) ,[editor settings](https://www.mintlify.com/docs/editor/settings#require-review-before-publishing) , and[roles](https://www.mintlify.com/docs/dashboard/roles) docs for details.


Reviews and expanded roles are available on Enterprise. If you're not on Enterprise yet,[talk to our team](https://www.mintlify.com/contact/sales) .
